extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, students of short fiction, librarians, and bibliographers
extracted.subtask_description: Bibliographic and critical evaluation of short-story volumes (including translations and collections), with indexing conventions and criteria for judging technique, translation, educational value, and literary significance. Includes guidance on what the index covers and how distinction is marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk indicates distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: An asterisk before a title indicates distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the index to mark volumes or stories of special merit; readers should treat starred items as notable or recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This list includes single short stories, collections of short stories, and a few continuous narratives based on short stories previously published in magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index covers standalone stories, collected volumes, and some connected narratives; it also lists volumes announced for upcoming publication even if not yet appeared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation fidelity / accurate rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations should be faultlessly rendered by a stylist who seeks to set down the exact shade of the critic's meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate translators on fidelity to nuance and idiom; high-quality translation preserves subtle critical or stylistic meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation quality can obscure or reveal art
rubrics_metrics.description: Poorly ('wretchedly') translated texts may obscure the underlying art, while good translations allow the original technique and art to be perceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors must separate the translator's failings from the original author's merit; negative judgments may be due to translation rather than source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polished technical craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories may not be 'literature' in a high sense, but exhibit a 'hard polished technique' — a competent, highly disciplined craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical polish (tight construction, effective devices) is a defendable quality; such technique can be compared to known exemplars (e.g., Poe) and is useful to students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic/melodramatic intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories may be 'frankly melodramatic' and 'wring the last drop of emotion and sentiment out of each situation presented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a descriptive stylistic register: melodrama can be a deliberate technique producing strong emotional effect, but may be viewed as less 'literary' by some critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to arrest reader's attention
rubrics_metrics.description: A desirable quality is that 'there is no story which does not arrest the attention of the reader.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether narrative, tone, or technique consistently engages and holds a reader; attention-arresting power is a positive indicator of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational value for students of technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Volumes may be 'valuable to students of short story construction' and include critical apparatus suitable for study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess collections for pedagogical usefulness: presence of introductions, historical/critical notes, biographical material, and exemplars of craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative revelation via dialogue vs. statement
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may 'present his characters more directly, and achieve his revelation through dialogue rather than personal statement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate method of character revelation—showing through dialogue/action is often praised over explicit authorial statement; note which method is employed and its effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to distill essence from simple material
rubrics_metrics.description: Some writers 'out of the simplest material... have extracted an exquisite spiritual essence, and held it up quietly so as to reflect every aspect of its value.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should value economical source material that is transmuted into deep thematic or spiritual resonance; subtlety and quiet revelation are praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical roundedness and developmental promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories can be judged as 'most completely rounded from a technical point of view' or as indicating 'the way toward future development.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between pieces that are technically complete and those that, while less finished, show promise or signal a writer's evolving strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic flawlessness vs. popular appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The art ... is flawless' even if a volume 'will not attract a large public.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics should separate aesthetic quality from commercial prospects; high artistry can exist without broad popular appeal and may still be recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic value and suggestion over explicitness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairy tales and legends that 'suggest more than they state' and possess 'a certain symbolic value' are artistically valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which stories use symbolism and implication rather than explicit explanation; subtle, suggestive works are to be valued for depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on motive rather than surface plot
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer may be 'less interested in the surface movement of plot than in the relentless search for motive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stories for psychological or motivational depth beyond mere plot mechanics; emphasis on motive can mark literary seriousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative/editorial completeness for anthologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections should aim for representative coverage (e.g., inclusion of major figures); omission of key authors (Sologub) is noted as a deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors/compilers are judged by how complete and representative their selections are for the field or national tradition they survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for technical inadequacy in young traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: When introducing a 'young tradition' (e.g., Romaic fiction), it is 'necessary to allow more than usual for technical inadequacy, but the substance... is sufficiently remarkable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply contextual standards: be more forgiving of formal/technical faults in emerging literatures if substantive originality or cultural importance is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful transfer of poetic style in translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translators may 'successfully transfer' the poetry of style to English; this is a distinct positive attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond literal fidelity, evaluate whether the translator conveys the original's poetic tone, atmosphere, and stylistic texture into the target language.
